validation.typecheck: passed: compiler, tests and all examples

change: Text equality and switch cases accept runtime text on either side. A native regex replacement escapes the prefixed runtime RHS, then constructs an absolute anchored pattern for the existing equality backend. Compile-time constants retain their original emitted actions.

verifiedShortcut.name: TS-Dynamic-Text
verifiedShortcut.completion: Every expected result appeared in order. After the last Done, play was available again in the shortcut editor with no error.
verifiedShortcut.importComparison: All 292 imported actions read from the simulator database match the compiled output exactly.

nativeCoverage: Runtime self-equality and inequality with extra suffix across 26 values
Empty strings, regex metacharacters, backslashes, ICU quote markers and replacement-group-like text
Composed/decomposed Unicode, emoji, LF and CRLF
Six deliberately different runtime text pairs remain unequal
Case expression effects run in order until the first match
Changing the discriminant variable inside a case expression does not change the selected value
Fallthrough runs a later body without evaluating its case expression
Default is selected after checking unmatched dynamic cases
compilerCoverage: Left-to-right, once-only argument evaluation with awaited helpers
LHS snapshot before RHS side effects
Composition with negation, ternaries and short-circuit Boolean operators
Literal aliases, parentheses, templates and constant concatenation use the static path
Anchored pattern wiring and runtime escape-output references
Invalid mixed-category and non-strict text comparisons are rejected
All existing native fixtures retain their previous expectations, including the explicitly documented historical equality migration
limitations: Direct matchText remains affected by the previously documented native intent-resolution failure; this implementation does not use it.
Only strict text equality/inequality are supported, not locale-aware sorting or relational string comparisons.
Runtime escaping adds one native Replace Text action to each dynamic comparison; repeated comparisons incur that cost.
The native example covers helper/loop/dictionary text outputs; awaited case actions are additionally covered by IR semantic tests, not a separate device prompt scenario.
Physical devices, other OS versions and every Shortcuts capability remain unverified.
